experiment: SUPERSEDED diagnostic: active proxy workload versus application-idle Firefox WebSocket
limitations: Ten blocks per protocol are screening evidence, below the 30-block confirmatory inference gate.
Measurements use unshaped isolated WSL loopback, MTU 1500 and disabled offloads; WAN RTT/bandwidth behavior is not established.
H3 denotes the startup route. WebSocket uses H1 over TLS/TCP, not RFC9220 or the existing QUIC connection.
One WebSocket does not mean one physical flow; probe/failed flows are included in the observer and byte totals.
Whole uses a startup-plus-idle-WebSocket Firefox reference. Active-WebSocket camouflage is not established.
The new strict early-window schema and mixed native listener setup are not directly comparable with historical canonical default matrices.
Small-request overhead includes transport setup for a fresh inner TLS/H2 stream and the measured capture tail.

measurement_contract.early_views: Strict packet geometry and window aggregates only; no future TLS-record ordinal or QUIC-phase metadata.
measurement_contract.firefox_control: Verified same-base Firefox loads the same SPA/assets/20 API pairs and opens one real H1 WSS. All 40 reference sessions then remain application-idle with zero post-bootstrap WS cells. This does not test camouflage against an active or sustained realtime application.
measurement_contract.residual: Normalized passive distance; lower is better, not a detection probability.
measurement_contract.warm_wire_window: Separate per-stage capture including at least 200ms after validation and an observed drain nonce. Completion time excludes this tail; wire totals include it.
measurement_contract.whole: All origin TCP and QUIC packets within exactly two seconds after cold navigation dispatch. This is not the complete lifetime of a long-lived WebSocket.

provenance.capture_readiness: own auxiliary UDP nonce observed in actual pcap before work and before stop; auxiliary port never enters origin features
provenance.cold_window_enforcement: epoch-bounded editcap slice from navigation dispatch; original capture retained
provenance.denominators: native classic and native no-connect with identical inner HTTPS/H2 work; rate_loss=100*(1-old_time/new_time); traffic_excess=100*(new_IP_wire/old_IP_wire-1)
provenance.native_listener_topology: Both SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT listeners are configured in every native process; the selected ingress changes by arm. Classic H2 therefore uses the mixed-listener implicit first-buffer policy.
provenance.network: isolated loopback MTU1500 offloads disabled; unshaped
provenance.observer_unit: all TCP and QUIC traffic to origin port, chronologically merged; no loopback proxy/target traffic
provenance.reference_lifecycle: same-origin SPA bootstrap20 then H1 WSS; empty application capacity

superseded_because: Firefox controls opened WebSocket but sent and received zero post-bootstrap WebSocket application cells; proxy workloads were active.
Whole was a two-second prefix, not a completed bounded application session.
Small request measurements created fresh inner TLS/H2 connections rather than reusing an active application WebSocket.
Both native listeners were configured, which changed the classic H2 SOCKS baseline policy.
The tested build contained a mapped-WebSocket routing bug hidden by localhost; the later correction changes connection establishment.

native_functional: 40 simultaneous logical streams with at most 32 per carrier
